items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: And it was Roy Zimmerman, Monk Hazel, I think he's left us. Uh, Leon Primer and myself, and, uh, we liked the trombone, but we did the Dixieland tunes.

ctx.x: And, of course, the, the, the famous store really still has jazz, and the Paddock, to a certain extent, really. I mean, they're both, they are, in a sense, both the same. Paddock Club is... Or have they changed those places?

The Paddock Club has retained their policy throughout the years. Matter of fact, I believe the Paddock was instrumental in setting the jazz reaction off on the, uh, off on the jazz trend, or what there was, off on Bourbon Street. But even before that, 1947 or 1948, uh, Leroy Primer had a club, St. Louis and Bourbon, the 500 Club. And while he presented shows, while he presented shows, he did a, the house policy was for, to have a show. And then the stage would push, push back under the bandstand, and we played…
No, no, it was at the 500 Club. Oh, this was at the 500 Club. This was before you opened your place.
